analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata. AddonPeerPolicy.swift:57-87 authenticates same-EUID peers using kernel audit tokens, signed identity/team requirements and hardened-runtime flags; its extra identity is DEBUG-only. ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift:65-117 binds IPC holds and subsequent access to the authenticated identifier. Holds introduce reversible admission closure, bounded inference draining/cancellation, model unloading, persistent restart state and machine-lock-dependent lease expiration (199-394). Autopilot/ProviderLoop+AutopilotBusy.swift:15-16 preserves a busy condition during holds. Coordinator/CoordinatorClient+Registration.swift:43-46,124-147 advertises busy on registration and only with draining heartbeats; encoding fallback still preserves draining status. The bounded CoordinatorClientCodec.swift patch forwards the new optional field, but full source was not supplied.
No concrete security regression is established here. No visible changes expose prompts, keys or tokens, alter encryption/cache scope, or grant serving authorization. Relevant contracts include TB-002/TB-010 availability interactions, TB-003 local-operator limits, TB-007/T-010 cancellation and T-028/T-041 memory/cache lifecycle, and TB-011/T-053 authorization continuity.
Integration must verify AddonIPCServer framing/resource limits and authentication timing, AddonHoldStore/paths and mailbox filesystem validation, lease bounds and machine-lock observations. Also examine beginServingDrain/resumeAfterAddonHold and all admission/load paths to establish that release cannot bypass current authorization or race outstanding unloads. At AddonHold.swift:259-266, held can be reported with retained models: verify the add-on's consumer contract treats this as admission closure, not guaranteed memory reclamation. Confirm startup ordering, reconnect busy-field interpretation and cancellation/native-retirement behavior with their implementations. These are unresolved cross-file contracts, not evidence of missing controls; this source pass does not establish deployment compatibility or a new billing/exposure failure.
